title.narrative: Policy and technical advice on the beneficial use of dredged materials in Colombia, including nature-based solutions

description.narrative: This project, financed through the Partners for Water Programme, focuses on policy- and technical advice for the beneficial uses of marine dredged sediments, including nature-based solutions (NbS).The core objective of the project is to provide a set of practical rules and parameters for beneficial use of dredged materials.The Media library on this page contains the final reports.Activities and deliverables1. Knowledge transfer on Dutch dredging practicesSummarises how the Netherlands governs, assesses, and monitors marine dredging through a purpose-based regulatory framework, clear institutional roles, strict sediment testing, and climate-adaptive approaches that support nature-based solutions.This activity's report describes Dutch regulatory structures, environmental criteria, threshold-setting methods, and adaptation/financing strategies related to dredging and dredge sediment reuse.DeliverableInformation, experiences, and lessons learned in the licensing, operation, monitoring and control of maritime dredging activities in the Netherlands, as well as in the determination of requirements to approve in this country the uses of marine dredged sediments. 2. Quality requirements for sediments globallyProvides an overview of international methods used to set sediment quality guidelines, compares threshold values across countries, and highlights challenges such as detection limits, climatic differences, and the limited global focus on beneficial reuse.This activity's report covers global analytical frameworks, compares procedural approaches internationally, and evaluates threshold values used in the Netherlands, Florida, and Brazil in relation to Colombia's context.DeliverableAnalysis of parameters and procedural steps of the Netherlands and other countries, to determine quality requirements of marine dredged sediments for their beneficial uses. Including lessons-learned for apporting to the determination of threshold values in Colombia aimed at beneficial uses of marine dredged sediments. 3. Sediment quality analysis in Barranquilla port areaAssesses the physical and chemical sediment conditions in the Barranquilla access canal and deposition zone, identifying substances of concern, major data gaps, and the need for improved sampling, monitoring, and Colombia specific thresholds.This activity's reports evaluate sediment data from Barranquilla, compares findings with international thresholds, identifies uncertainties, and provides recommendations for future assessments and guideline development.DeliverableAssessment of the quality of dredged marine sediments in the port area of Barranquilla. 4. Procedural guidelines for beneficial uses of dredged material in ColombiaPractical guidance on how dredged material can be managed and reused in Colombia in a safe and beneficial way. It focuses on rules and responsibilities, technical considerations, and social aspects, drawing on international experience and adapting it to the local context, with particular attention to the port area of Barranquilla.This activity report outlines how dredged material is currently managed in Colombia and how it can be safely and beneficially reused. It also presents a practical approach that links the quantity and quality of dredged material with local environmental and social needs, using a clear decision tree to determine whether material can be reused or must be safely disposed of to support sustainable dredging operations.DeliverableFormulate procedural guidelines to determine feasible and suitable uses of dredged marine sediments in Colombia, including nature-based solutions. 5. Case study for the beneficial use of dredged sediments in BarranquillaPresents how Nature based Solutions (NbS) can use dredged material from the Port of Barranquilla to provide effective environmental protection. It demonstrates that the port's large dredging volumes and generally suitable sediment quality can be transformed into sustainable solutions. Beneficial uses of dredged material ;such as coastal protection, submerged wave attenuation structures, and mangrove restoration; can deliver combined environmental, social, and economic benefits.DeliverableDevelopment of a theoretical case study for the use of dredged marine sediments from the port area of Barranquilla, for the execution of environmental protection works through NbS.Consortium• Arcadis is the leading global natural and built asset design and consultancy firm, working in partnership with their clients to deliver exceptional and sustainable outcomes through the application of design, consultancy, engineering, project, and management services.• Fundación Herencia Ambiental Caribe (FHAC) engenders sustainable development through the use and protection of the environment and natural, cultural, and social resources, emphasising community participation processes, and strengthening identity and culture.• JESyCA is a Colombian engineering and technical consultancy firm focusing on hydrology, hydraulics and environmental engineering in river, coastal and water resources related media.• NETICS is a leading innovative research and consultancy agency in civil engineering and is internationally regarded as the expert in the field of reuse and construction with dredged material.Counterparts• The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO) – Partners for Water.• The Netherlands embassy in Bogotá, Colombia.• Ministerio de Transporte (Mintransporte).• Departamento Nacional de Planeación (DNP).• Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible (Minambiente).
